newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS sees good Swiss business in 2 years.
newsitem.headline: CS sees good Swiss business in 2 years.

text.p: CS Holding expects its beleaguered domestic market in Switzerland to rebound in two years' time, chief executive Rainer Gut said.
"We are completely convinced that money can be made in this area as well," Gut told CASH TV when asked in a rare interview if the relatively small Swiss market was still attractive.

"We have set ourselves clear guidelines. Our competitors have said they have done the same. In two years we will have a very satisfactory Swiss business, rounded out by the acquisitions of the past few years."
Gut said CS Holding, whose restructuring into the Credit Suisse Group with clearly defined business lines will take effect on January 1, had for the most part wrapped up its sweeping revamp.

"The big scene is over, but I think no vital, flourishing company can say it is over (for good). But in the next two years we will certainly have a lot to do," he said, forecasting the new structure would be fully functioning by the end of 1998.

Gut said he thought all three big Swiss banks -- including Union Bank of Switzerland and Swiss Bank Corp -- would be able to maintain their international position in investment banking, although this required large investments.
"All three are certainly big enough. The question is how strongly each has the will to invest the necessary funds. As it appears now, all three are completely committed in this direction," he said.
Asked if all three would offer the same range of services in five years as they do now, he said he would rather not say too much on the subject.

"My view is well known, that basically the restructuring going on -- not just in Switzerland but in Europe as well -- will see national consolidations first before big cross-border consolidation takes place. But time will tell."
He said Swiss banks had to concentrate on international markets for investment banking because the domestic market was of limited importance.
"The world is of a completely different dimension," he said. "We have to concentrate on positions in main markets, to play a leading role in large mergers and project finance."
Gut, who is stepping down as chief executive at the end of the year but remaining chairman, made clear he would not leave the group entirely to new chief executive Lukas Muehlemann.
"I am convinced we will be a good team. But I am an active chairman and I am looking forward to making the CS Group with Lukas Muehlemann the world's leading bank."
